name: substr-search
axis: indexOf: first occurrence of a 12-char needle in a 1M-char text
notes: n = searches performed (PASSES * NN). Eight of the sixteen needles contain an uppercase Q, absent from the lowercase input, so they force a full 1M-character scan; the other eight hit near the front. Python needs NO reduction here - str.find is a C routine, so this is the one benchmark where the interpreter floor is not a floor. VL's indexOf takes no start offset, so 'find all occurrences' cannot be written without quadratic re-slicing.

audit.startupFloor: THREE of four columns are under the 200ms floor: rust 41.4ms (16% launcher), deno 139.0ms (14%), python3 140.7ms (9%); VL 1067ms. PASSES=240 would put rust at ~195ms and VL at ~4.3s if the measurement stage wants a startup-clean rerun; expect must then be re-recorded. measured empty-program startup on this box (min-of-5, taskset -c 2): rustc-O binary 6.8ms, deno 19.3ms, python3 12.5ms, `vl run <prebuilt.wasm>` 10.6ms.
audit.fairness: All four call the language's own builtin (Rust str::find, JS String.indexOf, Python str.find, VL String.indexOf), so this is a builtin-quality comparison, not builtin-vs-handwritten. Confirmed fair.
audit.protocol: ADVERSARIAL AUDIT, measurement protocol: (1) VL must be measured from a PREBUILT module — `vl run <src>` carries compile time, measured at 10-390ms (collections/map-string 1.47s prebuilt vs 1.86s from source = 27% compile; arrays/struct-aos 1.63s vs 1.92s). (2) This box swings up to 2.5x under contention even with taskset: recursion/flatcall's Rust binary read 2.53s in a sequential sweep and 0.996s as min-of-5 alone; recursion/fib's Rust read 2.02s while a second timing job ran and 0.53s alone. Every number must be min-of-N with EXCLUSIVE use of the box. (3) The known top-level-binding globals cliff is largely GONE at HEAD (#1321): measured locals-vs-globals 1.00-1.63x (f64-accum 1.63x and i64-accum 1.43x are the only real ones; fill-sum 1.05x, reverse-inplace 1.00x, map-i32 1.17x, struct-field 0.99x, char-scan 1.08x, token-count 0.95x). flatcall/flatcall-inlined/treewalk/ackermann/deeprec/mutual/tailcall spell their hot loop at TOP LEVEL while arith/* and collections/* wrap it in `function main()`; verified this no longer biases them (flatcall top-level 1.477s vs in-a-function 1.470s).
